title: Perspective, stereographic and orthographic projections compared
purpose: Project one rotated 4D polytope three ways side by side (stereographic edges as true circular arcs) and measure what each map keeps: straight lines, circles, parallels and angles. Reads built-in polytopes or any fourd_polytope/v1 JSON record.

parameters.meaning: tesseract, 16cell, 24cell, 5cell or a polytope JSON path
spacing of the views in circumradii

contract.coordinates: x, y, z, w; the three views sit along glTF x (perspective, stereographic, orthographic), +Y up

limits: Each view is scaled so its farthest vertex sits at the circumradius, which hides the real size differences between the projections. Stereographic arcs are polylines of a few segments (6 by default), so they approximate the circular images. Angle errors are measured at vertices only. The stereographic view refuses a vertex at the projection pole; choose a rotation that moves it. Input records must be convex polytopes centred near the origin for the circumsphere to make sense.
technique_references: stereographic projection of the 3-sphere (conformal, circle preserving)
great-circle arcs as radial images of chords
